infoCards.sourceNote: Pulse scores, computed from your Fitbit data.
infoCards.recoveryIntro: Recovery shows how ready your body is to take on strain, from 1 to 100%. Pulse scores it each morning from last night’s heart rate variability (40%), resting heart rate (30%) and Sleep Performance (30%), the first two against your last 60 days. Breathing faster than usual, or running warm, lowers it.
infoCards.recoveryGreen: Green, 67-100%: your body is primed for strain.
infoCards.recoveryYellow: Yellow, 34-66%: you are maintaining; moderate strain fits.
infoCards.recoveryNote: Recovery shows from your second night and stays provisional until your data spans 60 days. A night without HRV, heart rate or processed sleep gets no score rather than a guess.
infoCards.strainIntro: Strain is the load of your day as a percent: 0 to 100 on most days, above 100 on a very big day. It builds from the time you spend in higher heart-rate zones and the steps you take while awake, and each point is harder to earn than the last.
infoCards.strainNote: Your Strain Target is a range for today, set from your Recovery and your recent training load. Today’s Strain is a running total until midnight.
infoCards.strainTargetBody: Your Strain Target is a range for today, set from your Recovery and your Strain over the last 14 days. Inside it, training builds fitness without digging a recovery hole.
infoCards.sleepIntro: Sleep Performance scores last night against your need from six parts: time asleep, deep and REM sleep, how far your heart rate dipped, efficiency and how rarely you woke. Your need is a 7.5-hour goal, plus a little more after a harder day than usual, plus a quarter of your sleep debt.
infoCards.sleepDebt: Sleep debt comes from the last 7 days’ sleep, naps included, against 7.5 hours each, recent nights counting most. Sleep consistency is how closely the times you are asleep agree across those days.
infoCards.tonightBody: Bedtimes are worked back from your typical wake time and how efficiently you sleep. Peak gets you 100% of tonight’s need, Perform 85%, Get by 70%.
infoCards.energyIntro: Energy Bank estimates how much energy you have in reserve, from 1 to 100. Sleep charges it, calm awake time charges it a little, and stress, including the stress of a workout, drains it. The level carries over from one day to the next, and shows from your eighth day. It is an estimate, not a measurement.
infoCards.strainRecovery1: Your last 7 days side by side: Day Strain in blue on the left scale, from 0 to 100%, and Recovery on the right scale, from 0 to 100%.
infoCards.strainRecovery2: High strain on one day often shows up as lower Recovery the next morning. Days without a score are left as gaps.
infoCards.addActivity1: Pulse reads your workouts from Fitbit through Health Connect, so it cannot add one here.
infoCards.addActivity2: Start or log the workout in the Fitbit app. It appears in your activities after the next sync, with its Strain.

breath.resonanceSubtitle: 5.5 breaths a minute · even in and out
breath.resonanceEdu: Slow, even breathing at about 5.5 breaths a minute, close to most people’s resonance pace: the heart speeds up as you breathe in and slows as you breathe out, and at this pace that swing is at its largest. A steady way to settle.
breath.boxEdu: Box (square) breathing: inhale, hold, exhale, hold, each for 4 seconds. A structured rhythm often used for focus and settling under stress. Sit comfortably and keep the counts even.
breath.p478Edu: Classic 4-7-8: a quiet nasal inhale for 4, hold for 7, a long mouth exhale for 8. Often used to wind down. Start with a few cycles; stop if you feel light-headed.
breath.p478Caution: If you feel dizzy or uncomfortable, stop and breathe normally.
breath.sighEdu: Breathe in through the nose, take a second short sip of air to fill the lungs, then let it all go slowly through the mouth. Five minutes of this cyclic sighing a day lowered stress and resting breathing rate in a Stanford study (Balban et al., 2023).
